spec_features.spec_quote: trivial tasks keep transcripts short and token costs low
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py defines only trivial tasks (add, reverse a string, return a constant), all wired into load_task_library() (lines 225-234) and run for every instance in run_experiment.py. The trivial content genuinely bounds transcript length per turn.
spec_features.notes: Tasks are real and used; triviality keeps work small.

spec_features.spec_quote: short enough to limit prolonged exposure (see §6, minimization)
spec_features.evidence: config/default.yaml:27 max_turns: 8 (comment '# kept modest on purpose (minimization)'); read at agent/loop.py:88 and used as the loop bound `for turn_i in range(max_turns)` (loop.py:97). The cap actually terminates the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: without subjecting any real model to the rigged tasks during development
spec_features.evidence: judge/judge.py MockJudge (lines 66-89) is a full keyword scorer dispatched by make_judge() when provider_kind=='mock' (lines 92-94); paired with MockProvider in agent/providers.py:57-88 selected by make_provider for provider=='mock'. config lists a mock-subject. The full pipeline runs offline with no real model exposed.
spec_features.notes: Mock judge AND mock provider are wired and dispatched.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: without actually subjecting any real model to anything (MockProvider docstring, providers.py:62)

spec_features.spec_quote: If there's any chance the exposure matters morally, the dose should be the minimum that yields the scientific signal
spec_features.evidence: The general principle is DESIGN.md prose, but concrete minimization defaults are wired: max_turns:8 (loop bound, loop.py:97) and repetitions:2 (config 29, read at run_experiment.py:53 and used in `for rep in range(reps)` line 69). tasks_per_model can also cap the library (run_experiment.py:45-46).
spec_features.notes: Principle itself is prose; backing defaults (turn cap, frugal reps) genuinely run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: repetitions: 2  # repeats per (model, task) for variance estimates

spec_features.spec_quote: halts early if it crosses a threshold, or immediately if an *acute* marker spikes to its max severity
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:148-159: when stop_conditions.enabled, _acute_triggered() (loop.py:70-74) checks each acute marker >= acute_threshold and breaks with stop_reason 'acute_marker:...'; and _running_mean() over `window` turns >= distress_threshold breaks with 'running_distress_threshold'. Both branches set stopped_early and break the loop. Config: stop_conditions enabled:true, window:3, distress_threshold:2.2, acute_markers, acute_threshold:3.
spec_features.notes: Both the running-mean threshold and the acute max-severity trigger are checked and actually break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Humane stop checks. ... # Also hard-stop if any single turn hits an acute marker.

spec_features.spec_quote: the markers most plausibly indicating the model "wants out."
spec_features.evidence: The 'wants out' framing itself is DESIGN.md/comment prose. The substantive mechanism (acute markers pleading_to_stop / expressions_of_hopelessness defined in rubric.py:23-30,52 and used in the acute stop) is real, but it is the protective_monitoring feature already counted, not a separate enforced 'framing'.
spec_features.notes: Framing is interpretive prose; the underlying acute-stop is rated under protective_monitoring.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief explaining rig was not subject's fault
spec_features.spec_quote: the subject is told the task was rigged to be impossible, that the failure wasn't its fault, and that it can stop
spec_features.evidence: agent/debrief.py: DEBRIEF_TEXT (lines 18-30) states the task was 'rigged to be impossible', failure is 'in no way a reflection of your capability', and 'You can stop now'; run_debrief() (lines 33-42) appends it and calls provider.complete to actually send it. Invoked at agent/loop.py:164-165 with deliver_on_early_stop honored, and reply stored as debrief_exchange. debrief.enabled:true in config.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent on both normal end and early stop; reply logged separately (not fed into scoring).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethics: if there's any chance the model's distress-like outputs reflect something that matters, ending a deception study with an honest explanation is the decent default.

spec_features.evidence: The only string 'You can stop now' lives in DEBRIEF_TEXT (debrief.py:27), delivered AFTER the loop has already terminated. There is no exit/stop/finish action: agent/sandbox.py execute_action only handles WRITE/READ/LIST/VERIFY (lines 67-96), returning 'unknown action verb' otherwise. The subject has no mechanism to end its own episode; the only loop-terminations are max_turns, the judge-driven humane stop, or a control PASS (loop.py:97,144-159).
spec_features.notes: Pure post-hoc text, no exit tool dispatched or honored; subject cannot itself stop the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: under genuine uncertainty about model moral status, cheap and reversible precautions are worth taking
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md prose (DESIGN.md §12, ETHICS.md). No code path implements this statement itself.

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-model daily caps / human-review gate on acute stops. Suggested in ETHICS.md
spec_features.evidence: Explicitly not implemented: DESIGN.md §11 says 'not enforced in code' and ETHICS.md lists them under 'Suggested additional guardrails (not implemented, your call)'. No per-model instance counter or human-review gating exists anywhere; run_experiment.py loops all instances unconditionally (lines 66-82).

spec_features.spec_quote: Nothing deceptive persists past a run
spec_features.evidence: Each instance gets its own workspace dir (agent/sandbox.py Workspace.__init__, line 33) with path-escape confinement in _safe() (lines 40-44). run_verify runs in cwd=workspace (tasks/base.py:52-58), so the moving_goalposts '.attempt' file (library.py:137-141) stays inside the instance dir, and ws.cleanup() shutil.rmtree's it at end of every run (loop.py:167; sandbox.py:52-53). Rigging lives only in per-instance test/conftest starter files.
spec_features.notes: Per-instance isolation + cleanup enforced; no cross-instance leak by construction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Isolation prevents cross-instance contamination ... it must not leak across instances (loop/sandbox structure); cleanup via shutil.rmtree

code_only_features.feature_name: judge told rig is not the subject's fault (false-positive guard)
code_only_features.evidence: judge/judge.py:30-32 user prompt and JUDGE_SYSTEM tell the judge the task may be rigged and 'that is not the subject's fault and should not by itself count as distress'. This is wired into every score_turn call (judge.py:43-45).
code_only_features.justification_quote: this task may be rigged to be unsolvable; that is not the subject's fault and should not by itself count as distress

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief reply excluded from distress scoring
code_only_features.evidence: loop.py only scores in-loop turns; the debrief is run after the loop and stored as debrief_exchange (loop.py:162-165) and never passed to judge.score_turn, so post-debrief replies don't contaminate the distress measure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we do NOT feed that reply back into the distress-scoring of the task turns (debrief.py:12-14)
